correctness.rationale: A meet homomorphism L->2 either has empty preimage of 1, i.e. constant 0, or a nonempty upward meet-closed filter; finite filters have a unique least element, so exactly n principal-filter thresholds plus constant zero. Boolean coordinates are independent. For each join-irreducible j with unique lower cover j_*, any threshold separating j,j_* must be j, proving necessity that all r thresholds occur. They suffice because every finite lattice element is join of join-irreducibles below it, and occurrence-coordinate vector preserves that incidence. Inclusion-exclusion counts all e-tuples containing every distinguished threshold. Boundary r=0 (one-element lattice) not claimed to have minimal positive e=0; e>=1 formula remains valid. Independent direct meet-map enumeration on B2 (e=1,2,3 gives hom 5,25,125, emb 0,2,24) and nondistributive M3 (e=1,2 gives hom 6,36, emb 0,0) corroborated counts but the all-lattice proof is structural. Toth-Waldhauser Theorem4.1 explicitly identifies the polymorphism-homogeneous application.
